## V5 audit completed; corrected paper available

**[Read the corrected v5 paper: v0.5.1, q < 2,000](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/tag/v0.5.1)** ·
**[Download the corrected PDF](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/download/v0.5.1/tenth-discriminant-v0.5.1.pdf)**

V5 has passed a **manual mathematical audit with exact computational
checks**. This is not formal verification. V0.5.1 applies the audit's
minor wording correction in §6.2: the decreasing upper bound is
`110.001 log(R)/R`. The certificate already used that bound, so
`q < 2,000` and all numerical results are unchanged.

[Audit finding and correction](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.5.1/versions/v5.1/AUDIT.md).
The earlier papers, tags, and downloadable assets remain unchanged.

### Original v0.5.0 notes (status at publication)

**`q < 2,000`**, halving the v4 analytic cutoff.

**[Download the eleven-page proof](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/download/v0.5.0/tenth-discriminant-v0.5.0.pdf)** ·
**[Download the source and verification bundle](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/download/v0.5.0/tenth-discriminant-v0.5.0.zip)**

The new argument averages Green's derivative determinant inequality
over its size parameter, then compares the resulting prime sum with
the Euler product of primitive quadratic norms. This accounts for
composite norms discarded by the earlier point-count estimate.
Euler summation controls the norm series and its derivative.

The paper cites the independently verified
[v4 result](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/tag/v0.4.0)
for `q >= 4,000`. The rest of the argument is self-contained relative to
its stated classical inputs, including the determinant and resultant
proofs, the new averaging and Euler-product comparison, and numerical
formulas with explicit error bounds.

All **37 exact arithmetic checks** pass, certifying a gap greater than
**0.017** uniformly on `2,000 <= q <= 4,000`. The programs also pass
**62,880** retained finite determinant cases and a new comparison of
**10,000** primitive-norm coefficients with Euler factors. An exhaustive
scan checks the **249** remaining candidate integers below 2,000 and
confirms the nine surviving discriminants by reduced-form enumeration.

**Independent mathematical review of v5 is pending.** V4 has passed
independent verification. The finite computations and arithmetic
certificate do not establish the general v5 proof. Codex developed
the new derivation, paper, and verification programs.

analytic identities remain external inputs. No Heegner method or
computed zero-free region for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions is used.
Earlier papers, tags, and downloadable assets are unchanged. This is
an AI-assisted research draft, published as a prerelease for review.
